tier_reason: First-party README table against encoding/hex. The benchmark code is public (hex_test.go: BenchmarkEncode/BenchmarkRefEncode and BenchmarkDecode/BenchmarkRefDecode, with identical setups calling ref "encoding/hex"), but no CPU model, Go version or flags are given, so it is tier C. An independent 2026 CI run in go-simd/hex (a competing 1-star package, CPU model not given) corroborates the win, but it is not a well-known suite and does not lift the tier.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README benchmark table (committed 2016-11-11; unknown CPU, GOMAXPROCS 8, Go version unstated) with its own speedup column: Encode/1k 11572.80 vs encoding/hex 451.49 MB/s (25.63x); Decode/1k 6093.43 vs 245.43 MB/s (24.83x); encode ranges from 2.08x (15 B) to 31.17x (16k), decode from 4.26x (14 B) to 44.70x (128k); Encode/128M 4793.16 vs 457.13 MB/s (10.49x); Decode/128M 5397.68 vs 143.72 MB/s (37.56x). An independent re-measurement in the go-simd/hex README (1 MiB random buffer, GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest AMD EPYC, GOAMD64=v1, median of 6, recent Go) gives encode 18785 vs 980 MB/s (19.2x) and decode 9566 vs 2095 MB/s (4.57x) for tmthrgd/go-hex against current encoding/hex.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 26 stars, 2 forks; archived 2025-09-11 (repo description says '[Abandoned]'); a pinned dependency of go-simd/hex (go.mod), and search results show it vendored in GoToSocial's tree (snippet only)
corrections.caveats: The README numbers were committed on 2016-11-11 (Go 1.7 era), not about 2017. CPU model, Go version and flags are not given; only GOMAXPROCS 8 can be read from the -8 suffix. The asm was regenerated afterwards without re-running the table (go1.8/go1.10 updates, PEXTRB workaround 77b1f74, AVX/SSE split, pre-SSE4.1 fallback). None of those commits is a correctness fix of the measured path. Current golang/go encoding/hex Decode uses a reverseHexTable lookup, and stdlib throughput has risen since then. The independent go-simd/hex CI run (competitor package, 1 star, CPU model not given) measures only 4.57x for decode and 19.2x for encode at 1 MiB against current stdlib, so the README's 25-45x decode ratios are stale. Only amd64 builds get SIMD: dispatch is on AVX or SSE4.1, not AVX2, so the kernels are 128-bit. Non-amd64, gccgo and appengine builds use hex_other.go, the old Go-Authors scalar code. go-simd/hex reports that path's arm64 decode as about 9.7x slower than its own fallback, which tracks encoding/hex, so it is slower than the stdlib there. The decode benchmark input is built by an overlapping in-place Encode; it is still valid hex and identical for both rows. The repo is archived and called abandoned by its author, so no fixes will come. Licence is BSD-3-Clause. asm_gen.go also carries Wojciech Mula's Simplified BSD (BSD-2) notice, and hex.go/hex_other.go carry the Go Authors' BSD notice, all OSI.

notes: The README numbers match the record. The README itself prints the speedup column, so the ratios are first-party rather than derived. The main shortcoming: the numbers are from 2016 on an unstated CPU and Go version, and a 2026 third-party run (go-simd/hex README, competitor) shows decode is only 4.57x faster than today's encoding/hex, not 25-44x; encode stays about 19x. The non-amd64 fallback is slower than the current stdlib. This is not a duplicate of any catalog entry (no prior go-hex or go-simd/hex record found in data/).
